```xml
<Project>

    <!-- Production -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions" Version="8.0.1" />

    <PackageVersion Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="NSubstitute" Version="5.1.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

```xml
<Nullable>enable</Nullable>
<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
<EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
<Company>Contoso</Company>
<Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
```

```xml
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
```

```xml
</Target>
```

```xml
<Project>
```

Core, Services, and Api all have `<DocumentationFile>` in a **second** `<PropertyGroup>` separated from the main one. This is unnecessary fragmentation — properties should be grouped logically into as few PropertyGroups as needed (typically one unless gated by different conditions).

data.content: Now I notice the `Directory.Build.props` has a logic issue — the `IsPackable` default is `false`, but the conditional `GenerateDocumentationFile` checks `'$(IsPackable)' != 'false'`. Since the default sets it to `false`, the doc generation condition will never be true for source projects that don't override it. The source projects don't set `IsPackable` at all, so they'll inherit `false`. Let me fix this — source projects should not be `IsPackable=false` by default. Instead, I'll use a different approach:
